title: CMAS Purchase and Installation Agreement – Valley Precision Grading, Inc. – Hoover Elementary School Turf Replacement Project – Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a CMAS Purchase and Installation Agreement by and between the District and Valley Precision Grading, Inc., for the latter to remove existing turf, supply and install the new PIVOT Performance Turf and maxFLO (shock pad) turf system with integrated stripping for the Hoover Elementary School Turf Replacement Project, in the not-to-exceed amount of $248,062.00, with work scheduled to commence upon District’s Notice to Proceed and shall terminate upon completion of the Work for the Project, within two hundred calendars days from the date of the Notice to Proceed.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Pays Valley Precision Grading up to $248,062 to replace the turf at Hoover Elementary
summary: Valley Precision Grading will remove the old turf at Hoover Elementary and install a new turf and shock-pad system. The district is buying through a state contract list, the California Multiple Award Schedules (CMAS), instead of running its own bid. Work starts when the district gives notice to proceed and must finish within 200 calendar days.
outcome_action: Adopted

title: General Services Agreement – A-Tech Consulting – Lead Abatement Group 1 - Division of Facilities Planning and Management

outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Amendment No. 2, Amendment for Project Assignment – Anthonio, Inc. - Bret Harte Middle School Asphalt Replacement Project –Division of Facilities Planning and Management

title: Grant Award - California Opportunity Youth Apprenticeship - Talent/Human Resources Department
official_text: Acceptance by the Board of Education of California Opportunity Youth Apprenticeship (COYA) Grant from the California Department of Industrial Relations (Division of Apprenticeship Standards) in the amount of $600,000.00 to sustain and expand the Early Educator Apprenticeship Pathway, for eligible 16-24 year old youth, by strengthening a clearly articulated youth-to-career continuum that connects high school students to a registered apprenticeship in Early Childhood Education, pursuant to the terms and conditions thereof, for the period July 1, 2026 through December 31, 2028.

title: Memorandum of Understanding – AC Transit – Restoration of Line 31 Service - Skyline High School – Talent/Human Resources Department

vendor_name: Jon K Takata Corporation dba Restoration Management Company
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Amendment No. 1, Services Agreement - Claremont Partners, Inc. - Risk Management Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1, Services Agreement 2025-2026 by and between the District and Claremont Partners, Inc., Fresno, CA, for the latter to continue to provide the unchanged services, including employee health benefits communications and secretarial services, to the labor-management Health Benefits Governance Board ("HBGB"), by extending the term of the agreement from July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026 to June 30, 2027, at the unchanged cost of $36,000.00 annually, via the Risk Management Department.  All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
headline: Extends Claremont Partners' health benefits communications contract a year at $36,000 per year
summary: The district is extending, by one year to June 30, 2027, its agreement with Claremont Partners for employee health benefits communications and secretarial support to the labor-management Health Benefits Governance Board. The yearly cost stays at $36,000 and the services are unchanged.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Excess Workers’ Compensation Coverage and Excess Property and Liability Coverage - Premium Payment - Fiscal Year 2026-2027 - Risk Management Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of payment of membership contributions (premium) to Public Risk Innovation, Solutions, and Management (PRISM), a Joint Powers Authority (“JPA”), for Excess Workers’ Compensation Coverage, for Fiscal Year 2026-2027, in the amount of $888,000.00 and payment of premium to Northern California ReLiEF (“NCR”) JPA, administered by Keenan & Associates, Torrance, CA (Broker), for Excess Property and Liability Coverage. for July 1, 2026 through July 1, 2027, in the amount of $4,318,365.00, respectively.
headline: Pays $4.32M for excess property and liability coverage and $888,000 for excess workers' compensation
summary: The district will pay $888,000 to the PRISM joint powers authority for excess workers' compensation coverage for fiscal year 2026-27. It will also pay $4,318,365 to the Northern California ReLiEF joint powers authority, through broker Keenan & Associates, for excess property and liability coverage from July 1, 2026 to July 1, 2027.
vendor_name: Northern California ReLiEF (administered by Keenan & Associates)
outcome_action: Adopted

title: Claims Adjusting and Administrative Services Contract, Subrogation Agreement and Data Sharing Agreement - George Hills Company - General Counsel
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Claims Adjusting and Administration Service Contract (CAASC) * (inclusive of Attachments: A; A-1; A-2; B, C, D, E) by and between the District and George Hills Company, Inc., Rancho Cordova, CA, a Property and Liability Third Party Administrator (TPA), rejecting all other bids, for the latter to provide liability and property claims adjusting services to the District, at a cost not to exceed $400,000.00 per fiscal year, subject to a 3% annual Escalator, for the term of June 1, 2026 through and including June 30, 2028, with an option for renewal of the CAASC for one-year periods thereafter; and of a Data Sharing Agreement (DSA), by and between Parties, for the same term as the CAASC, and the option to renew DSA for one year periods thereafter, pertaining to the District’s transmission of data to the second Party (George Hills Company) and the protection by the second Party of such data, pursuant to the terms and conditions of the DSA; each, via the Risk Management Department.
headline: Hires George Hills Company for liability and property claims adjusting, up to $400,000 per year
summary: George Hills Company, a third party administrator (TPA), will handle the district's liability and property claims for up to $400,000 per fiscal year, with a 3% annual increase. The term runs June 1, 2026 through June 30, 2028, with one-year renewals possible. The text says the board is rejecting all other bids. A data sharing agreement covers the same term.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement - The Institute for Excellence In Education - Charter Schools Office
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement by and between the District and with The Institute for Excellence In Education, Mt. Pleasant, MI, for the latter to provide use of the Epicenter platform, including setup and technical support, that will allow for the Office of Charter Schools (OCS) to efficiently assess and track data and documents related to charter governance, equitable admissions and enrollment processes, fiscal health and management, enrollment and attendance reports, teacher credentialing, charter board management, and dozens of other compliance-related documents that OCS collects and reviews annually, as delineated in Exhibit A of the Agreement, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, via Office of Charter Schools, for the period of July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, in an amount not to exceed $39,700.00.
headline: Ratifies $39,700 for the Epicenter platform to track charter school oversight data
summary: The Institute for Excellence In Education will provide the Epicenter software platform, with setup and technical support, so the Office of Charter Schools can track data and documents on charter governance, admissions, finances, enrollment, attendance and teacher credentials. The term is July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027.
vendor_name: The Institute for Excellence In Education
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement - Centurisk - Risk Management Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement by and between the District and Centurisk, for the latter to conduct an onsite inspection to perform an inventory verification of machinery and equipment fixed assets with an original cost of $500 and greater; provide District the data to the District for proper accountability and stewardship of capital assets, assist with the financial reporting requirements of GASB 34, and external audit requirements, with tasks more specifically detailed in Exhibit B of the Agreement, for the term April 10, 2026 through June 30, 2027, at a cost not to exceed $249,500.00.
funding_source: Fund 67 Resource 9031- Self Insurance Property & Liability
headline: Pays Centurisk up to $249,500 to verify the district's machinery and equipment inventory
summary: Centurisk will inspect school and district sites and verify the inventory of machinery and equipment that cost $500 or more. This supports accountability for assets, financial reporting rules and the outside audit. The service period began April 10, 2026, before board approval, and runs through June 30, 2027.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report
